def-td-driven-finite-path-model.physical_scope: A finite-microstate, finite-stage, single-reservoir protocol model with externally changed energies and discrete bath transitions; it does not assert that a material apparatus has this dynamics.

def-td-driven-finite-path-model:
## Definition

Take $\Omega$ to be a finite nonempty microstate set as in [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: distinct elements count as distinct microstates, and the physical energy values are finite and measured in joules in the declared rest frame. Fix an integer $m\ge1$ and stage energy functions $E_k:\Omega\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ for $k=0,\ldots,m$, with the energy offsets fixed by the declared protocol model. Fix inverse temperature $\beta>0$ in joules$^{-1}$. The finite partition sum and canonical probability vector at stage $k$ are $Z_k=\sum_{i\in\Omega}e^{-\beta E_k(i)}$ and $\pi_k(i)=e^{-\beta E_k(i)}/Z_k$. Since $\Omega$ is nonempty and finite and each energy is finite, $0<Z_k<\infty$ and $\pi_k$ is a strictly positive probability vector.

A transition kernel at stage $k$ is a matrix $K_k(i,j)\ge0$ with $\sum_{j\in\Omega}K_k(i,j)=1$. In the forward stage order, the energy changes instantaneously from $E_{k-1}$ to $E_k$ while the state is still $i_{k-1}$; the subsequent bath transition samples $i_k$ using $K_k(i_{k-1},i_k)$ at fixed energy $E_k$. A path is $\omega=(i_0,\ldots,i_m)\in\Omega^{m+1}$. For an initial law $\mu_0$, its path probability is $P_F(\omega)=\mu_0(i_0)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_{k-1},i_k)$.

Work on the system is positive when energy is supplied to it, and heat into the system is positive when a bath transition raises its energy. Define $W(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^m[E_k(i_{k-1})-E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})]$ and $Q_{\mathrm{in}}(\omega)=\sum_{k=1}^m[E_k(i_k)-E_k(i_{k-1})]$, both in joules. Define $F_k=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_k$ and $\Delta F=F_m-F_0=-\beta^{-1}\log(Z_m/Z_0)$. These are finite-model quantities; their physical interpretation is conditional on the adopted preparation and transition assumptions.

def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model.physical_scope: Finite-state, time-homogeneous continuous-time rate models and their reversible discrete transition-kernel analogue; the definition does not assert that a physical system follows either model.

def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model:
## Definition

A finite rate model consists of a finite nonempty state set $S$ and rates $q_{ij}\ge0$ in seconds$^{-1}$ for $i\ne j$. Set $q_{ii}=-\sum_{j\ne i}q_{ij}$. A row probability vector is $p=(p_i)_{i\in S}$ with $p_i\ge0$ and $\sum_i p_i=1$. Its time-dependent law $p(t)$ follows the continuous-time master equation $\dot p_i=\sum_{j\ne i}[p_jq_{ji}-p_iq_{ij}]$. A strictly positive normalized vector $\pi$ is a detailed-balance law when $\pi_iq_{ij}=\pi_jq_{ji}$ for every distinct pair. Its undirected rate graph has an edge $\{i,j\}$ exactly when $\pi_iq_{ij}>0$; detailed balance makes this equivalent to $\pi_jq_{ji}>0$.

For a discrete transition kernel $K$ on a finite state set, $\pi$-detailed balance means $\pi_iK(i,j)=\pi_jK(j,i)$ for every pair. If $\pi$ is strictly positive, this identity pairs the supports of forward and reversed transitions. A rate model or a reversible kernel is a mathematical/physical model class; no observed trajectory is asserted by the definition.

post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation.physical_scope: The start of the specified finite-state protocol is modeled as a canonical preparation at one positive reservoir temperature; preparation success and equilibration are not derived.

post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation:
## Postulate

For a protocol of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], fix a bath temperature $T_b>0$ kelvin and set $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T_b)^{-1}$ in joules$^{-1}$, using the exact constant and SI conventions of [[def-td-si-quantities]]. The finite-state clause of the adopted [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] then gives the stage-zero law $\pi_0(i)=e^{-\beta E_0(i)}/Z_0$; adopt that the initial microstate is drawn from this law, so $\mu_0=\pi_0$. Here $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and $E_0(i)$ is finite, so $0<Z_0<\infty$ as required by that clause. This is a model premise about the preparation distribution. It does not follow from the finite partition-sum definition, does not assert that an arbitrary system equilibrates in finite time, and does not report a measured preparation. The countable-state and measure-integral branches of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]] are not used.

post-td-stationary-bath-kernel.physical_scope: The transition matrices of the specified finite-state model preserve each stage's canonical probability vector; no universal Markov approximation or physical thermalization theorem is asserted.

post-td-stationary-bath-kernel:
## Postulate

For the protocol in [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], adopt, at each stage $k=1,\ldots,m$, the stationarity condition $\sum_{i\in\Omega}\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)$ for every $j\in\Omega$. This says that if the bath transition begins with law $\pi_k$ at fixed energy $E_k$, it ends with the same law. It is a physical modeling assumption for this protocol family, not a consequence of the transition-kernel definition and not an assertion that the kernel mixes every initial law to $\pi_k$.

post-td-linear-ornstein-uhlenbeck-bath.physical_scope: One-dimensional overdamped motion in a harmonic potential, with constant positive mobility and stiffness, one fixed positive bath temperature, additive Gaussian white-noise modeling, and no inertia or memory.

post-td-linear-ornstein-uhlenbeck-bath:
## Postulate

For the harmonic potential $U(x)=kx^2/2$ with position $x$ in metres, stiffness $k>0$ in joules per square metre, constant mobility $\mu>0$ in square metres per joule-second, and a bath at fixed $T_b>0$ kelvin, adopt the one-dimensional overdamped model $dX_t=-\gamma X_t\,dt+\sigma\,dB_t$, interpreted through the integral equation of [[def-tdmath-ornstein-uhlenbeck-equation]], with $\gamma=\mu k$ in seconds$^{-1}$ and $\sigma^2=2\mu k_{\mathrm B}T_b$ in square metres per second. Here $B$ is standard Brownian motion with its stated filtration and increment hypotheses, and the bath noise is independent of the initial preparation. This Einstein noise relation and the linear Markov model are physical assumptions. They do not follow from equilibrium thermodynamics alone and do not report a measured spectrum or calibration.

def-td-finite-memory-reset-model.physical_scope: A finite-state memory and retained register with a specified probabilistic reset map; the definition does not assert a particular apparatus, reset dynamics, or measured work.

def-td-finite-memory-reset-model:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a finite memory-state set and $R$ a finite retained-register set. A joint preparation is a probability law $p(m,r)\ge0$ with $\sum_{m,r}p(m,r)=1$. Write $a_r=\sum_m p(m,r)$ and, for $a_r>0$, $q(m|r)=p(m,r)/a_r$. Use the finite Shannon entropy in nats and the conditional entropy $H(M|R)$ exactly as defined by [[lem-tdmath-conditional-memory-entropy]]. For a fixed target memory state $m_0$, a reset is the endpoint map $p'(m,r)=\mathbf 1_{\{m=m_0\}}a_r$: it places the memory at $m_0$ while leaving the register marginal unchanged. The definition alone assigns no physical entropy, work cost, heat transfer, or implementation.

pthm-td-finite-pathwise-first-law.physical_scope: An exact energy bookkeeping identity for every path of the stated finite-state, finite-stage model; it is not a claim that all heat or work processes are represented by this model.

pthm-td-finite-pathwise-first-law:
## Statement

For every path $\omega=(i_0,\ldots,i_m)$ of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], the endpoint energy change is $E_m(i_m)-E_0(i_0)=W(\omega)+Q_{\mathrm{in}}(\omega)$, with the stated sign convention.

pthm-td-markov-relative-entropy-and-conv.physical_scope: A finite, time-homogeneous continuous-time rate model satisfying detailed balance; convergence is asserted only when its positive-rate graph is connected, and no general continuum or non-Markovian relaxation theorem is claimed.

pthm-td-markov-relative-entropy-and-conv:
## Statement

Let $S$ have $N\ge2$ states, positive detailed-balance law $\pi$, and connected undirected rate graph as in [[def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model]]. For every strictly positive initial probability vector $p(0)$, the master equation has a unique strictly positive probability solution $p(t)$ for all $t\ge0$. The relative entropy $D(p(t)\Vert\pi)=\sum_i p_i(t)\log(p_i(t)/\pi_i)$ is nonincreasing, and $p_i(t)\to\pi_i$ for every state. No monotonicity of Shannon entropy $-\sum_i p_i\log p_i$ is asserted.

pthm-td-finite-jarzynski.physical_scope: An exact ensemble identity for a finite state space, finite protocol, canonical initial law, and kernels preserving each stage's canonical law; no claim is made for general stochastic processes or for any individual path.

pthm-td-finite-jarzynski:
## Statement

For the forward path law of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], under [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]] and [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]], the finite expectation satisfies $\mathbb E_F[e^{-\beta W}]=Z_m/Z_0=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$. This is an ensemble identity; it does not say $W=\Delta F$ on each path.

pthm-td-finite-crooks.physical_scope: A path-reversal identity for a finite-state protocol whose stage kernels are reversible with respect to their positive canonical laws; it does not extend to arbitrary driven systems without matching support and reversal assumptions.

pthm-td-finite-crooks:
## Statement

Assume the setup of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], the canonical initial law of [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]], the stationarity model of [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]], and, additionally, $\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)K_k(j,i)$ for every $k,i,j$. For every forward path with positive probability, define its reverse probability by $P_R(\omega^R)=\pi_m(i_m)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_k,i_{k-1})$. Then $P_R(\omega^R)>0$ and $P_F(\omega)/P_R(\omega^R)=e^{\beta(W(\omega)-\Delta F)}$. Consequently, at each work value $w$, $P_F(W=w)=e^{\beta(w-\Delta F)}P_R(W_R=-w)$. The reverse protocol first applies the stage-$k$ reverse transition at fixed $E_k$, then reverses the quench $E_k\to E_{k-1}$; its work is $W_R(\omega^R)=-W(\omega)$.

pthm-td-ornstein-uhlenbeck-thermal-fluct.physical_scope: Conditional predictions of the specified one-dimensional linear Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model after stationary Gaussian preparation; not empirical claims and not general laws for arbitrary baths.

pthm-td-ornstein-uhlenbeck-thermal-fluct:
## Statement

Under [[post-td-linear-ornstein-uhlenbeck-bath]], prepare $X_0\sim N(0,V)$ independently of future Brownian increments, where $V=k_{\mathrm B}T_b/k$. Then the conditional linear model has stationary covariance $C(\tau)=Ve^{-\mu k|\tau|}$. With angular-frequency convention $S(\omega)=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_{\mathbb R}C(\tau)e^{i\omega\tau}\,d\tau$, its spectrum is $S(\omega)=\mu k_{\mathrm B}T_b/(\pi[(\mu k)^2+\omega^2])$. For every averaging time $T>0$, $\operatorname{Var}(T^{-1}\int_0^T X_t\,dt)\le 2k_{\mathrm B}T_b/(\mu k^2T)$. These are model predictions, not reported observations.

pthm-td-qualified-landauer-reset.physical_scope: A conditional endpoint work bound for a finite memory reset with fixed retained-register marginal, a positive-temperature ideal bath, the stated entropy identification, and no endpoint energy change; no universal cost per bit or measured work is asserted.

pthm-td-qualified-landauer-reset:
## Statement

For the reset model of [[def-td-finite-memory-reset-model]], assume (i) the memory-register thermodynamic entropy is $k_{\mathrm B}H(M,R)$ at both endpoints, (ii) a single ideal reservoir remains at fixed $T_b>0$ kelvin and receives heat $Q_b$, (iii) the memory-register endpoint energy is unchanged so the adopted first-law convention gives work on the system $W=Q_b$, and (iv) the total entropy change obeys $\Delta S_{\mathrm{memory+register}}+Q_b/T_b\ge0$. Then $W\ge k_{\mathrm B}T_bH(M|R)$. Equality is not asserted without a separately specified reversible implementation.

pthm-td-mean-dissipation.physical_scope: An inequality for the ensemble-mean work in the finite protocol under the Jarzynski model assumptions; it is not a per-path second-law inequality and is not an empirical statement.

pthm-td-mean-dissipation:
## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]], the mean work obeys $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. The conclusion concerns the path ensemble only; individual paths may have $W<\Delta F$.

ex-td-finite-quench-work-fluctuation.physical_scope: A calculated two-state hypothetical protocol example; it is not an experiment and makes no claim about a measured system.

ex-td-disconnected-markov-relaxation.physical_scope: An exact three-state finite-rate calculation showing why the connectedness condition in the convergence theorem is needed; not empirical data.

ex-td-biased-bath-shannon-entropy-decrea.physical_scope: An exact two-state finite-rate calculation distinguishing Shannon entropy from relative entropy to a biased stationary law; no empirical claim.

ex-td-ornstein-uhlenbeck-spectrum.physical_scope: A calculated stationary spectrum and averaging bound in the adopted scalar harmonic Ornstein-Uhlenbeck model; no measured spectrum is asserted.

ex-td-biased-memory-reset-bound.physical_scope: A symbolic finite-memory calculation under the reset theorem's physical assumptions; it is not a measured reset process.

ex-td-correlated-memory-zero-conditional.physical_scope: A calculated finite correlated-memory model illustrating the theorem's retained-register condition; no measurement or reset apparatus is described.
